inventory_findings.message: Vale 3.14.1 is installed but no .vale.ini or .vale/ config was found in this repository; EN D3/D4 Vale mechanics are skipped for this scan.

findings.message: Opening German guillemet „ paired with ASCII closing " instead of typographic “; first word of quoted speech must also be capitalised.
findings.evidence: „ein Redakteur, der still umschreiben kann, was er findet" ist die falsche Form.
findings.suggested_resolution: Change to: „Ein Redakteur, der still umschreiben kann, was er findet“ ist die falsche Form.

findings.message: Two quoted phrases open with „ but close with ASCII " instead of typographic “.
findings.evidence: „lektoriere diesen Post" oder „prüfe die Docs auf Lesbarkeit" aus
findings.suggested_resolution: Replace both closing " with “: „lektoriere diesen Post“ oder „prüfe die Docs auf Lesbarkeit“ aus.

findings.message: Quoted phrase opens with „ but closes with ASCII " instead of typographic “.
findings.evidence: einen deutschen Satz zu „reparieren", indem es ihn englisch macht

findings.message: Informal du-address (dir) on an explanation-mode page; spec requires impersonal voice for explanation/reference/glossary pages.
findings.evidence: Falls dir das Plugin noch nichts sagt:
findings.suggested_resolution: Recast as impersonal: "Wer das Plugin noch nicht kennt:" — also apply at line 66 ("bevor er dich erreichte").

findings.message: Second instance of informal du-address (dich); consistent with line 17 but still violates the impersonal-voice rule for explanation-mode.
findings.suggested_resolution: Replace with impersonal phrasing: "bevor er den Leser erreichte" or "bevor dieser Beitrag veröffentlicht wurde".

findings.message: Opening paragraph runs ~4 sentences in one block; splitting after the motivation clause eases entry for explanation-mode readers.
findings.evidence: Jeder Beitrag auf dieser Seite ist KI-entworfen und danach von Hand kuratiert. Dem Entwerfen vertraue ich; das Kuratieren will ich nicht
findings.suggested_resolution: Break into two paragraphs at the em-dash or after the semicolon to separate motivation from tool introduction.

findings.message: Paragraph contains ~4 sentences with a long embedded quoted clause; dominant lever is ASL.
findings.evidence: Der Grund für die Trennung: „Ein Redakteur, der still umschreiben kann, was er findet“ ist die falsche Form.
findings.suggested_resolution: Split after "nicht nur durch guten Willen." to separate justification from the operational consequence.

findings.message: Domain term "Register-Drift" used without definition on first use; not all technical readers have an editorial-theory background.
findings.evidence: undefinierten Jargon und Register-Drift abzuklopfen ist genau die Arbeit
findings.suggested_resolution: Add an inline gloss: "Register-Drift (unbeabsichtigte Tonanpassungen im Textverlauf)".

findings.message: Opening paragraph contains ~4 sentences in one block; splitting improves entry for explanation-mode readers.
findings.evidence: Every post on this site is AI-drafted and then curated by hand. The drafting I trust; the curation I don't want to do by eyeball
findings.suggested_resolution: Break after "The drafting I trust;" to separate motivation from tool introduction.

findings.message: Paragraph packs ~4 sentences covering three distinct tools (LIX, Vale, LanguageTool); LWP is the dominant lever.
findings.evidence: D1 leans on LIX, a readability metric computed the same way for English and German, with a target corridor that depends on the page type.
findings.suggested_resolution: Split after "depends on the page type." so the Vale/LanguageTool sentence stands as its own short paragraph.

findings.message: Paragraph contains ~4 sentences; embedded quoted rationale and its mechanism crowd one block.
findings.evidence: The reason for the split is that "an editor that can silently rewrite what it finds" is the wrong shape.
findings.suggested_resolution: Break after "wrong shape." to isolate the architectural justification from its runtime consequence.

findings.message: Closing paragraph contains ~4 sentences; the long third sentence (corridor, stable ID, git trail) drives ASL above the comfortable reading band.
findings.evidence: It applies the same corridor to every paragraph, records each finding with a stable ID so a dismissal I made last week still holds
findings.suggested_resolution: Split before "and leaves an audit trail in git" to form two shorter sentences.

findings.message: Term "register drift" used without definition on first use; readers without an editorial background may not know it.
findings.evidence: reading every paragraph for sentence length, undefined jargon, and register drift is the work I'm bad at
findings.suggested_resolution: Add an inline gloss: "register drift (unintended shifts in tone or formality across a document)".

findings.message: "unified diff" used without definition on first use; a subset of audience A may not be familiar with the term.
findings.evidence: It walks the findings in severity order and shows me a unified diff for each.
findings.suggested_resolution: Add a short parenthetical: "a unified diff (a standard patch format showing changed lines in context)".
